title.narrative: Acting Now Rwanda

description.narrative: Africa is currently facing severe food insecurity, with low agricultural productivity being one of the root causes. Factors such as limited access to quality inputs, inadequate extension services, lack of finance, and post-harvest handling issues contribute to low agricultural productivity. Food insecurity is exacerbated by economic, political and demographic shocks, including the war in Ukraine, which has caused rising food and energy prices and lower yields in 2022. Climate change further intensifies food insecurity, with extreme weather events such as droughts and floods impacting crop and livestock production and access to markets. Conflict and insecurity are also major drivers of acute food security issues, leading to population displacement and disrupted livelihoods, depriving people of income sources. Action is needed to relieve acute food insecurity, whilst at the same time structurally transforming food systems. Farmers’ Organisations and its member farmers play a critical role in obtaining this, as they contribute not only to food production, but also to sustained economic growth and climate change mitigation. The Acting Now for Food Security and Resilient Food Systems programme, with funding from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (specifically IGG), builds upon its existing strategic partnership with DDE by reinforcing and expanding its efforts on food security, contributing to a more measurable impact on SGD 2 (Zero Hunger). It contributes to improved food and nutrition security (FNS) at the individual farmer level and fosters systemic change in the food system through a total of 82 Farmer Organisations in Burkina Faso, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya and Rwanda. As per Agriterra’s core business, Acting Now will work with and through Farmers’ Organisations and cooperatives to build resilient food systems and to make a sustainable change in the lives of smallholder farmers and their communities. Key Activities Acting Now aims to boost productivity, improving incomes and sustainable land management practices through the following key activities: - Trainings and peer-to-peer activities on FNS related topics, such as Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), Regenerative Agriculture, productivity increase at specific value chains and production of compost and bio-inputs. - Establishment of demo plots to promote and train farmers on new or improved farming practices and technologies. - Offering sustainable services through a tailored approach per country that ensures access to seeds, fertilisers, planting material, agri-inputs and extension services. - Strengthening extension services by co-financing the salary of extension officers and agronomists at the FO through Agriterra’s Jobs Jobs Jobs approach - Co-financing investments and innovations to boost agricultural productivity and food security.

title.narrative: Farmers indirectly trained by Agriterra to support FNS interventions

description.narrative: Active farmer members of FOs who received extension services from their FO and with Agriterra’s contribution in view of promoting FNS outcomes. Extension services include all interventions aimed at structurally and/or systemically contribute to improving farmers’ agricultural performance (i.e. aimed at long-term outcome results, as formulated in the IGG-FNS framework). This can for instance be because the intervention covers multiple aspects of agricultural performance (inputs, farming techniques, market potential) and/or there is regular follow-up. Specificity of these activities is that they fall within the cooperative’s responsibility and are overseen by the cooperative, not Agriterra.

title.narrative: Farmers supported

description.narrative: Active farmers as directly reported by the farmers’ organizations clients of Agriterra. Active farmers are farmers with formal membership and active economic relationship during the year with the Farmer Organization (FO), e.g. paying membership fees, selling crops to or buying agricultural inputs and other goods or services from the FO, holding savings accounts or loans with the FO, etc. Therefore, active membership is defined from an economic point of view and not from a normative point of view (attending the AGM, voting, etc.).

title.narrative: Mobilised capital to boost agricultural productivity & food distribution

description.narrative: Economic value expressed in euros of all the financial contracts and equity agreements obtained by farmers’ organizations with the support of Agriterra. The capital mobilisation is attributable to Agriterra's support only if Agriterra's contribution can be demonstrated. Financial resources mobilized include economic contributions by members in the form of internal capitalization to their farmer’s organisations triggered by the support of Agriterra and financial contracts obtained by FOs with the support of Agriterra. Capital from FOs matching Acting Now co-investments is not considered mobilized capital because additionality cannot be demonstrated. This capital can be reported upon separately, next to this indicator.

title.narrative: Farmers' Organisation supported

description.narrative: Farmers’ organizations (Primary & Secondary) supported at least one one-year project with the Acting Now Programme of Agriterra. These FOs become clients of Agriterra. A farmers’ organization is defined as a formal or informal (registered or unregistered) membership-based collective action group serving its members, whose livelihood (partly or in full) comes from agriculture (crops, livestock, fisheries, etc.). It might be an association, a federation, a cooperative, a union of cooperatives, an apex for lobby, or a private company owned by farmers.

title.narrative: New revenue generating activities at FO level

description.narrative: New revenue generating activities at FO level is a parent indicator overarching two child indicators: New Enterprise and Other New Revenue Generating Business Units: New Enterprises: New, expanded or improved factory, storage, machinery or transport facility intended to increase the value-added of the crops purchased from members or the quality or range of the services provided to the members, in the stage of completion, which has been facilitated with the support of Agriterra. Other new revenue-generating business unit: New revenue-generating business unit set up by the farmers’ organisation with the support of Agriterra, oriented towards boosting agricultural productivity of farmer members (i.e. intended to offer better services to farmer members) and which does not require an investment in fixed assets (e.g., agricultural input distribution unit, production of agricultural inputs unit, financial services unit, self-financed extension services unit, etc.).

title.narrative: Hectares of farmland directly reached aimed at improvement (structural/temporary) of agro-ecological sustainability

description.narrative: Number of hectares of farmland on which farmers directly trained by Agriterra in Acting Now and farmers with improved access to inputs and services that promote the Acting Now FNS outcomes report intending to apply the techniques taught during the trainings. Structural agro-ecological sustainability refers to: Hectares of farmland reached in a targeted way (i.e. farmland area reached is – or can be – known) with an intervention that structurally and/or systemically contributes to improving ecologically sustainable land use (i.e. aimed at long term outcome results, as formulated in the IGG-FNS framework). This can for instance be because the intervention covers multiple aspects of sustainable land use (soil fertility, biodiversity, crop rotation) and/or there is regular follow-up. Examples: targeted farmer training and inputs for climate-smart agriculture (CSA), integrated soil fertility management, crop rotation, erosion protection measures, (…) Temporary agro-ecological sustainability refers to: Hectares of farmland reached in a targeted way (i.e. farmland area reached is – or can be – known) with an intervention that temporarily and/or partially improves ecological sustainability. In other words, the intervention in itself cannot be assumed to lead to measurable (long-term) outcome results. Examples: providing access to digital weather forecast for specific farmers; onetime (group) training on land degradation, (…)

description.narrative: FTE employees hired by an FOs reached in the scope of an Acting Now project. A job created is attributable to Agriterra’s support only if Agriterra’s contribution can be demonstrated, e.g. through a financial contribution to the payment of the FTE’s salary.
